page: Google Cloud Platform c4n-highcpu-4 is a compute-optimized instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8581C processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, resulting in 2 threads per core. The instance is configured with 8 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and has zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

In benchmark evaluations, the c4n-highcpu-4 demonstrates strong single-core performance, highlighted by a Geekbench single-core score of 2228.0, placing it in the top tier. Single-threaded operations such as gzip compression at 34.85 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 15.13 GB/sec perform strongly. However, multi-core and memory-bound operations show limitations; the stress-ng multi-core CPU performance is relatively weak at 4403.68, and memory bandwidth tests, such as 32.55 GB/sec for large block read-only operations, fall into the lower performance tier. The CPU supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions for deep learning and cryptography acceleration.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c4n-highcpu-4 offers a specialized compute-to-memory profile that minimizes memory overhead costs for workloads that primarily demand raw single-threaded CPU speed. Given its high single-core performance but constrained memory bandwidth and multi-core scaling, this instance is best suited for single-threaded processing tasks, lightweight web serving, basic Redis key-value operations, and workloads utilizing vector or matrix instructions that do not require large memory footprints.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4n-highcpu-4 is an x86_64 compute-optimized server featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs and 8 GB of RAM, powered by an Intel Xeon 8581C processor running at 2.3 GHz. The instance lacks local storage and GPU accelerators, focusing its resource profile entirely on compute density with a 2.0 GB per vCPU memory ratio. Benchmark data reveals exceptional single-core capabilities, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2228.0 and strong single-threaded compression performance. Conversely, multi-core scaling and memory bandwidth are relatively weak, as evidenced by a 32.55 GB/sec uncached read speed. Equipped with Intel AMX and AVX-512 instruction sets, this server is highly efficient for compute-bound, single-threaded tasks, lightweight web serving, and basic vector math operations where memory capacity is not a bottleneck.
